page: Google Cloud Platform m4-megamem-224 is a memory-optimized server instance within the m4 family. It features 224 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. The instance is configured with 2976.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 13.29 GB per vCPU.

This server configuration does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met through external network-attached block storage. Additionally, the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Given the high density of memory relative to compute cores, this instance is designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. The lack of local storage and GPU hardware represents a clear tradeoff, focusing resource allocation entirely on memory capacity and CPU compute. Appropriate workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, and massive data analytics pipelines that require keeping large datasets entirely in system memory.
